 Advertisement Ravens QB Lamar Jackson ruled out for matchup with Bengals
 Advertisement Updated: 10:51 PM EDT Oct 24, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Kurt Knue Ravens QB Lamar Jackson ruled out for matchup with Bengals
 Updated: 10:51 PM EDT Oct 24, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Kurt Knue BALTIMORE — Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson has reportedly been ruled out for the team's divisional rivalry game against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday.
 According to NFL insiders that include NFL.com's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter, the three-time first-team All-Pro quarterback will remain sidelined this weekend as he continues to recover from an ankle injury.

— Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 24, 2026 
 This content is imported from x. You may be able to find the same content in another format, or you may be able to find more information, at their web site. Lamar Jackson has been downgraded to out for Sunday’s game against the Bengals.
— Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 24, 2026 
 The 29-year-old suffered the injury in Week 4 during the Ravens' game against the Tennessee Titans on Oct. 4. Ever since, Baltimore has struggled on the field in his absence, losing last week to the Cleveland Browns and narrowly escaping with a win in overtime against a shorthanded Atlanta Falcons team the Sunday before.
 During the Bengals' matchup with the Ravens, Cincinnati will be seeking to extend its record to 4-2, which is what all three of the other AFC North teams currently remain tied at going into Week 7.
 However, due to the early bye week, the Bengals currently sit at 3-2, putting them last in the division.
 Before the injury news came down, the matchup had been widely anticipated as the toughest test yet for Cincinnati's newly revamped defensive line, with Jackson named as the league MVP for the 2019 and 2023 seasons.
 However, Joe Burrow and the Bengals offense are still expected to be in for quite a defensive challenge from the Ravens on Sunday: As the Bengals take to the field at M&T Bank Stadium, it will mark the first time that Burrow will face off against Trey Hendrickson on an opposing team's defensive line. This comes after the star edge rusher, who led the NFL in sacks in 2024, left Cincinnati last year for Baltimore following a prolonged contract dispute with the Bengals front office.
 The game kicks off at 1 p.m. in Baltimore.
